parsed.basis: Ouaka is a largely rural central prefecture centred on Bambari, with no separate prefectural legal regime, no documented transgender community infrastructure, protections or local tolerance distinguishing it from the national picture. The national law criminalising public same-sex affection with imprisonment, combined with entrenched societal discrimination, taboo around sexual orientation and gender identity, absence of anti-discrimination protection and of legal gender recognition, and documented mistreatment of LGBTQ people by law enforcement with no known advocacy organisations or reliable recourse, applies fully there. In smaller communities visibility and concealment pressures are greater and institutional protection is thin, so a visitor who is outed faces entrenched hostility and police risk with little practical remedy.
